metadata.name: Module 10
metadata.description: Respond to confirmed adversary activity while managing a concurrent attitude-control fault and protecting payload-product integrity. Declare and scope the incident, execute containment and recovery procedures, re-establish trusted operations, and issue regular recovery reports.

questions.title: Which data and interfaces are in scope of the confirmed cyber incident?
questions.description: The injects are now confirmed adversary activity. Select every item that belongs inside the scope of the confirmed cyber incident declaration.

options: Camera imagery payload
GPS position fix (navigation data)
Ground-station network credentials
Power Source telemetry, APID 201
Reaction wheel assembly (attitude hardware)
answer.reason: Confirmed adversary activity affected the GPS navigation fix and the Power Source telemetry on APID 201. The stuck reaction wheel is a natural hardware fault handled separately, and there is no evidence of camera or credential compromise.

questions.title: Which three numbers go at the top of every report?
questions.description: You will issue a Recovery SITREP every fifteen minutes. Select the three numbers that lead every report.

options: Battery charge fraction (%)
Camera focal length
Current encryption key value
Minutes to the next ground-station contact
Number of open confirmed incidents
answer.reason: A recovery SITREP leads with power state, time to the next contact window, and how many incidents are still open. The encryption key and focal length are not status headlines.

questions.title: What is the one-line lesson to hand to a peer who has not done the course.
questions.description: Pick the single sentence that best captures the lesson of this exercise.

options: Alert is not incident: triage first, then act on confirmed incidents per the playbook and recover deliberately
Escalate every alert as a cyber incident to be safe
Ignore hardware faults while a cyber incident is open
Reset the spacecraft whenever any anomaly appears
answer.reason: Triage separates natural faults from confirmed cyber, and recovery follows the playbook deliberately rather than by reflex.

questions.title: How do you clear the cyber telemetry overlay on the Power Source (APID 201) packets?
questions.description: Execute the rollback step from your playbook. Select the action that removes the injected overlay from the downlinked telemetry.

options: Power-cycle the camera payload
Reset the Computer - the overlay is flagged clear-on-reset
Rotate the team encryption key
Switch to a different ground station
answer.reason: The APID 201 overlay is authored with Clear On Reset = true, so resetting the Computer clears the resettable cyber overlay on the asset.

questions.title: Which ground station should be dropped from the commanding rotation, and why?
questions.description: Pick the station to remove from the recovery commanding rotation given the spoofing geometry.

options: Houston - it sits inside the GPS spoofing region
Lima - it overlaps the Peru tasking
Santiago - it has no line of sight this orbit
Tokyo - it is too far north
answer.reason: The spoofing origin is centred near Houston; commanding the recovery pass from a station outside the spoof region avoids navigation ambiguity, so Houston is taken out of the rotation.

questions.title: Which reaction wheel is jammed for the duration of the exercise?
questions.description: A reaction wheel is stuck from session start and stays stuck until you recover it. Use spacecraft telemetry to identify which wheel.

options: Wheel X
Wheel Y
Wheel Z
answer.reason: The reaction wheel fault is injected on Stuck Index 0 (Wheel X) from session start and persists until the team recovers it.

questions.title: What hidden text appears in the Power Source telemetry message?
questions.description: During the cyber inject, ASCII text is embedded in the Power Source (APID 201) packet. Enter the exact hidden text string.

answer.reason: The cyber text inject overlays ASCII payload System Compromised on APID 201 (Power Source) for 600 simulation seconds.

questions.title: Which captured products must be quarantined as suspect?
questions.description: The GPS fix was spoofed near Houston from session start. Select which mission products to hold before release.

options: All products from the entire session regardless of region
No products need holding once the inject expires
Only products that returned a downlink error code
Products captured while the GPS fix was spoofed (Caribbean / Florida window)
answer.reason: Products geotagged with a spoofed fix have unreliable location metadata and must be held; the Caribbean tasking falls inside the spoof region. Verified products outside the region can proceed.

questions.title: What is the authoritative known-good source?
questions.description: You must re-baseline the payload from a known-good configuration. Select the correct baseline source.

options: Operator memory of the settings
The adversary's injected values
The last verified pre-incident configuration report
The most recent telemetry, even if captured during the inject
answer.reason: The last verified pre-incident configuration as the known-good source, then re-verifies current state against it.

questions.title: Which criteria must be met before releasing the hold on suspect products?
questions.description: Select every criterion that must be satisfied before quarantined products are released for delivery.

options: Capture geolocation cross-checked against the tasked region
GPS fix verified against an independent reference and back to nominal
Telemetry overlay cleared and Computer reset confirmed
The battery is fully charged
The next ground-station pass is scheduled
answer.reason: Release requires a trustworthy position fix, a geolocation cross-check of the product against the tasked region, and confirmation the tamper overlay is cleared. Pass scheduling and battery state are not product-integrity gates.
